biggest_catch: There is no single official list of every class action — you must match yourself to each case's own official settlement website before its hard deadline, and payouts are usually small and arrive months later.
catches: No single official database covers every class action — the FTC page covers FTC-administered cases only; other cases live on their own official settlement websites.
Third-party aggregator sites are leads only — always file on the official settlement website run by the court-appointed administrator.
Each case has a hard claim deadline; missing it means no payout.
Payouts are often small (single-digit to tens of dollars for consumer cases) and arrive months after the final approval hearing.
Scam sites mimic settlement notices — the FTC states it will never threaten you, demand money to release a refund, or promise a prize.

c1.evidence: FTC (U.S. federal agency) publishes the official active-refund-program list; individual settlements are run by court-appointed administrators (Epiq, Kroll, JND Legal Administration, Rust Consulting, Simpluris, Analytics Consulting).

c2.evidence: FTC page lists active refund programs with administrators and contact info; each settlement's official website publishes the class definition, claim form, and deadlines.

c3.evidence: Filing a claim is free; the FTC warns it will never ask you to transfer money to get a refund.

c4.evidence: Each program states its payout terms on its official settlement website; the FTC page currently lists active programs (e.g., Amazon Refunds Sep 2026, AT&T Data Throttling Aug 2026, Grubhub Refunds Aug 2026).

eligibility: Varies per settlement — you must fall inside the court-defined class (e.g., bought a specific product in a date range, used a service during a period).

steps: Go to https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/refunds and scan the Active Refund Programs table for a company or product you used.
For non-FTC class actions, search the web for the case name plus 'official settlement website' — open the administrator's site (Epiq, Kroll, JND, etc.), never a random blog.
On the official settlement website, read the class definition to confirm you qualify (dates, product, state).
Check the claim deadline and what proof is required (receipt, account email, or no proof needed).
Fill out the official online claim form with truthful information — false claims can be rejected and may lead to penalties.
Choose your payment method if offered (check, PayPal, Venmo, prepaid card).
Save your confirmation number and wait — payments typically arrive months after the final approval hearing.
timing: Varies by case; typically months after the final court approval hearing.
